title: Set browser startup policy from C#
goal: Manage Blazor startup and reconnection from C#.

selectionNotes: RC2 sharing: use uniform public policy.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: Server-side BrowserOptions requires ASP.NET Core 11; no net10 equivalent.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Matching Razor and browser assets; pinned RC2 compiled/executed.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Canonical sample language mode; the option assignments use ordinary C# syntax.

prerequisites: Blazor Web App with Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web, AddRazorComponents and blazor.web.js. AddInteractiveServerComponents/AddInteractiveServerRenderMode for circuits. WebAssembly/Auto additionally need the actual Microsoft.NET.Sdk.BlazorWebAssembly client project, host project reference, WebAssembly.Server/WebAssembly packages matching the framework, AddInteractiveWebAssemblyComponents/AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode and browser runtime assets. The complete setup is in Markdown.

WithBrowserOptions attaches endpoint metadata; ConfigureBrowser runs during request rendering with an HttpContext. Static lookup is BrowserOptions.GetBrowserOptions(context), not an HttpContext extension.
constraints: Final RC1 groups: InteractiveServer, StaticServer, InteractiveWebAssembly. Serializable data only; function callbacks remain JavaScript initializers. Server reconnection policy applies to circuits, including Auto while it uses Server; a WebAssembly instance has no server circuit to reconnect.

Pinned RC2 separate HTTP requests reproduced endpoint/component sharing (7 -> 1 -> 1). Apply a uniform non-secret application policy. Do not put user, tenant or request-specific values in shared endpoint options. This is a bounded local reproduction, not a framework-wide security conclusion or GA claim.

Component non-null values replace earlier endpoint values; omitted scalars retain them. TimeSpan serializes to milliseconds; PreserveDom serializes as negated disableDomPreservation. ConfigureBrowser is request rendering, not a live circuit-settings update.

Standalone WASM without an ASP.NET Core component endpoint does not acquire server options. .NET 10 uses valid startup JavaScript; it is only the previous-release comparison, not an older-target route for BrowserOptions.

Exact .NET 10/RC2 Server, WebAssembly and Auto startup and Server interruption/recovery are local Windows Chromium evidence. No other browser/OS, AOT, deployment, transport/auth-expiry policy, automatic circuit pause or GA execution is claimed.
